question: On the every-bar ladder the linear readings change: all five models INTERMEDIATE on every bar (linear were CONCENTRATED monthly; k90 5 -> 10); top 10 beat the full set significantly only for the ridge (p .030 / .361 / .522); top 5 keep 78-87% and are significantly worse for lasso and elastic net; the best linear rung is 10-20. How should A_fi:388-411, 01_introduction:133-136 and 09_conclusion:46-50 state the linear result (and the trees' 'other series add little', now p .008 / .005)?

solvers.answer: Every-bar numbers with their tests in the appendix; the introduction and conclusion say the linear models are at least as accurate with the top 10 and keep 'the signal sits in a few series'; the trees' remainder small but significant; 'do best with 10-20' dropped.

Same direction; the introduction and conclusion print the linear 104-115% next to the trees' 96-97% and keep 'sits in a few series'; the appendix prints every p-value; the trees' remainder is 'a small gain that is significant'.

Same direction; the introduction and conclusion print the linear range, carry no ridge p (it fails a Holm adjustment, 0.09), and say the gain sits in about 10 of the 46 series; the appendix states every test and the day-type split.

refutation.note: Numbers re-read from results/ablations_2014start_w3000/scores_fomcfix/ladall_readings.csv and ladall_scores.csv and matched to the EB macros: linear R10 115/105/104, R20 107/102/104, R5 87/84/78; p(10 vs full) 0.030/0.361/0.522 (DM all negative); p(20 vs full) 0.244/0.673/0.231; p(5 vs full) 0.084/0.007/<0.001 (DM positive); trees R10 97/96, R5 36/38, p10 0.008/0.005, p20 0.031/0.010, best rung 46; k90 = 10 in all five; elastic net QLIKE 0.176083 at k = 20 against 0.176133 at k = 10, the tie behind \ladderEBLinKstarRng = 10--20. The EB file's claim report marks two current linear claims FAILS. Holm over the three rungs gives the ridge's top 10 0.091, but ladder RULE section 6 prescribes the raw DM p of k = 20, 10, 5 and no DM test in the paper is adjusted for multiplicity (the only mention, A_econ.tex:699, says the strategies are not), so the appendix prints nominal p and the introduction and conclusion carry no p, as all three solvers propose. Refuted point: the evidence and author-record solvers keep 'the exogenous signal sits in a few series'. The pre-specified reading (results/ladder_2026-10-26/RULE.txt:116-121) calls k90 <= 5 concentrated and 10 intermediate; every model is intermediate on every bar; V4 allows verdict words only with a backing predicate. 'A few series' would claim the reading the ladder no longer gives, while 'no model is dense and weak' backs only 'rather than spreading thinly'. The referee's 'about \ladderEBTopK{} of the ... series' is adopted for the introduction and conclusion; 'about' reflects the rung grid (k90 lies above 5 and at most 10 for every model). git blame: the three passages are agent text (5554817, b0477ae), not protected by A4. No author message after 14:42 PDT on 29 Oct.

precedence_note: V6 (author, 29 Oct 12:51) governs the form: each significance claim is stated with its test, never as a clause-final tail. A1 (28 Oct 23:22) and the 'go' (28 Oct 17:04) govern the content: the every-bar numbers back the sentences. The ladder RULE's reading (section 6) decides the verdict words. No author decision on this wording conflicts.
final_answer: Conditional on Q-2026-10-29-30's switch; if that is vetoed, this item lapses and the monthly text stays. State the linear result as the every-bar numbers show it, each significance claim with its test and no clause-final verdict tails (V6): the top 10 series keep at least the full set's gain in all three linear classes, significantly more only in the ridge (nominal p, as everywhere else in the paper); the top 5 keep less, significantly less in the lasso and the elastic net; the pre-specified reading is intermediate in all five models. 'Concentrated' is no longer said of the ladder, and 'do best with N series' goes. The boosted trees' remainder beyond the top 10 is small but significant, with its tests; the forest's monthly result is one labelled sentence. The introduction and conclusion print the linear range next to the trees', carry no p-value, and say the gain sits in about \ladderEBTopK{} of the \rhldEBNSeries{} series instead of 'a few series'. The headings ('The gain is concentrated, not dense and weak'; 'The gain is concentrated') stay: they rest on the group ablations. The 'Ridge against lasso' bullet (A_fi.tex:403-408) is unchanged. Replacement text for 01_introduction.tex:133-138, 09_conclusion.tex:46-50 and A_fi.tex:385-414, and the generator's new macros and checks, are in actions[].detail; the old text is parked in dated comments.
answer_short: Ladder sentences on every-bar numbers: top 10 keep 96-97% of the boosted trees' gain and 104-115% of the linear models'; gain in about 10 of 46 series; 'concentrated', 'do best' dropped.
rationale: All three lenses agree on the content: every-bar numbers, no 'concentrated' for the ladder, no 'do best with', the trees' remainder stated as small but significant, every test printed in the appendix and none in the introduction or conclusion. They differ on wording; the decisive points were settled against the repo: the linear range is printed in the headline sentences (two of three, and V4 favours a number over 'at least as accurate'), no multiplicity-adjusted p is introduced (the rule and the paper use nominal DM p), and 'a few series' gives way to the referee's 'about ten of the 46', because the rule reads ten series as intermediate. Confidence 0.7: the content is settled; the exact phrasing is taste. T2 (taste, majority, refutation succeeded on one sentence). HIGH: introduction and conclusion. Consequence 4.

The linear sub-item (l.396-402, with the old post hoc sentence; update the dated comment at l.390-395) becomes:
  \item Linear models: the top 10 series keep \rhldEBLinRTenMin{}--\rhldEBLinRTenMax{}\% of the gain and the top 20
    \rhldEBLinRTwentyMin{}--\rhldEBLinRTwentyMax\%, so in each class both rungs have a lower loss than the full set.
    The top 10 are significantly more accurate than the full set in the ridge (DM $p = \rhldEBRidgeBarPTenFull$). In
    the lasso and the elastic net the difference is not significant ($p = \rhldEBLassoBarPTenFull$ and

The 'Ridge against lasso' sub-item (l.403-408) is unchanged. The closing paragraph (l.410-414) becomes:
  On every bar, then, each model's top 10 series keep at least \rhldRulePct\% of its gain and its top 5 do not

Asserts, so a rerun cannot silently falsify the new sentences (V4, V5): \rhldEBLinRTenMin and \rhldEBLinRTwentyMin above 100 and \rhldEBLinNRungsBelowFullMin equal to 2; the ridge's p(10 vs full) below 0.05 with a negative DM, the lasso's and elastic net's at or above 0.05; \rhldEBLinPTwentyFullMin at or above 0.05; the lasso's and elastic net's p(5 vs full) below 0.05 with a positive DM; \rhldEBLinRFiveMax below 100; \rhldEBTreePTenFullMax and \rhldEBTreePTwentyFullMax below 0.05 with positive DMs; the tree and linear k90 minima and maxima all equal \ladderEBTopK and every R_5 below the threshold; the LightGBM and XGBoost ordinary-day verdicts equal the three linear statement-day verdicts; the monthly forest verdict equals the monthly LightGBM and XGBoost verdicts.
